title: SubGuard: AI reads the fine print. PayPal enforces the outcome.
_actions: Each action is {"action": goto|click|hover|type|press|wait_for|wait|scroll_to|highlight, ...}. Targets are data-testid values; goto takes a path ({sub:<plan_key>} = the id of a subscription a scene's setup made), type takes text, press takes a key, wait takes seconds. "mock_only": true skips an action in sandbox mode.
_dates: {on:N} in on_screen / narration is the calendar date N days after a sign-up made today, as SubGuard writes it ("Nov 18"; the voice-over says "November 18"). Resolved when the video is checked, recorded and voiced.
_scenes: "separate": true records the scene after the main run (the build still puts it in scenes.json order); "setup" makes a subscription off screen first. "sandbox_subscribe": in sandbox mode, after the scene, the recorder registers the pre-approved subscription from `make seed --demo-subs` (the hand-recorded clip shows PayPal's window).
_clips: A scene with "type": "clip" is a manually recorded clip (demo-video/clips/, gitignored; see demo-video/README.md). build_video.py inserts it at that position, trimmed to its duration; it has no actions. check_scenes.py warns if the file is missing, and a mock build skips it.

scenes.on_screen: SubGuard reads the fine print on free trials, and uses PayPal to stop the charge you didn't agree to.
scenes.narration: SubGuard reads the fine print on free trials, and uses PayPal to stop the charge you didn't agree to.
Priya wants Penwright, a fictional AI writing app. Ten days free, nothing today. The real terms hide in tiny grey text and a folded Terms section.

She clicks PayPal, and SubGuard reads the fine print first: $24.99 a month after the trial, then $49.99. Act by {on:7}; the terms allow {on:8}. PayPal's plan confirms the charge. A hidden note to AI is ignored. She can let SubGuard send the email if she doesn't answer.
Then the real PayPal sandbox window: the ten-day trial, then $24.99 a month. She agrees, and PayPal confirms the subscription is active.

scenes.on_screen: Quillnote: the AI found it (act by {on:4}). The basic check missed it ({on:7}, too late).
scenes.narration: Why AI? Quillnote hides its notice period in prose: seventy-two hours. The AI says act by {on:4}. A basic rule check says {on:7}: too late.
Day five. SubGuard checks in by email, text and in the app. She's opened Penwright twice. SubGuard suggests cancelling, as advice. Priya decides.

scenes.on_screen: Cancelled in PayPal first. Then the email her terms require.
scenes.narration: She taps Cancel and confirms: no $24.99 charge on {on:11}. SubGuard cancels in PayPal first. Then AI drafts the email her terms require, quoting the clause word for word. She can edit it, then sends it; in this demo it's saved, not emailed. Back on her card, SubGuard reads PayPal live: cancelled.

scenes.on_screen: Every step logged: R1 her consent, R2 the safety timer
scenes.narration: Every decision is logged, hash-chained, with its rule: R1 for her tap. With no answer, rule R2 allows the Day 6 auto-cancel only after a warning.

scenes.on_screen: Day 11: first charge blocked. Scale: Fair Trial partners · one tap in PayPal · the PayPal wallet
scenes.narration: Day eleven, the first charge is due. SubGuard checks PayPal: no active subscription, so no charge can be taken. It scales three ways: Fair Trial partners, one tap in PayPal for everyone else, and next, the PayPal wallet itself.

scenes.on_screen: Charges avoided: $24.99 (up to $524.88 in year one) · MIT · github.com/vishvinsartech/Paypal-hackathon-idea-3
scenes.narration: $24.99 never charged. AI reads the fine print. PayPal enforces the outcome. Open source, MIT licensed.
